Table 1: Comparison of M3Exam with representative conversational-memory benchmarks. A. Round = average user–assistant rounds per session; A. File = average images and document files per session. MR = multimodal reasoning over visual evidence; SA = statistical analysis of multimodal graphs; FM = file management and retrieval; FR = file reasoning over document content. II = implicit information inference; TH = domain-specific thematic reasoning. ✓= supported; ✓✗ = partial / restricted; ✗ = not supported; ∼= N/A.

Figure 2: Overall pipeline of M3Exam, designed to evaluate multimodal memory ability in realistic scenarios.

Figure 9: Frontier-MLLM arena on M3Exam. We evaluate eight frontier closed-source multimodal LLMs—GLM5.1, Qwen3.6-Plus, Claude-Opus-4.6, Doubao-Seed-2.0, GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Kimi-k2.5 and Grok-4—as the answering model on M3Exam, scoring every model under the four metrics (EM, F1, BLEU-1 and LLM-J). Left: overall ranking, where each model is scored under a unified standard combining the four metrics. Right: per-metric breakdown, one radar per metric, where each hexagon spans the six question types that the metric is defined on and each model is drawn as one colored polygon.
